raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Skip unused text decoding for token-only gRPC generation. Also avoid unused stream decoders for control requests, one-shot detokenization, and health probes.

CPU-mock results with the same enlarged response queue in both builds:

- **Throughput: +10.9%** (819k → 909k tokens/s).
- **Frontend CPU per token: −9.6%** (6.893 → 6.230 µs).

Validation: 336 server tests pass; formatting, Clippy with warnings denied, and the diff check pass.

nodes.body: The health-probe note in the review is also addressed in 05d2b763: probes now use `OutputMode::TokenIds`, and both existing health-probe tests check that mode.

No correctness issues found. The token-only gRPC `generate` path never reads `text`, stop-token trimming and logprob-text decoding behave the same as before, and every other adapter keeps `TextAndTokenIds` via `Default`. The `detokenizer` and `grpc` tests pass (30/30) and clippy is clean.

The inline comments are one test gap plus cleanups. One more that isn't on a changed line:

- `rust/sglang-server/src/frontend.rs:280`: the health probe builds its `FrontendRequest` with `..Default::default()`, so it gets `TextAndTokenIds` and mints a `DecodeStream` on every `/health` call, even though its output is never read. Setting `output_mode: OutputMode::TokenIds` there would extend this optimization to the other token-only caller.

Nothing tests this passthrough. The new detokenizer test builds `DetokState` by hand and calls `new_decoder` directly, and the gRPC tests only assert `output_mode` on the intake request. If this arm regressed to `Default::default()`, every gRPC `generate` would quietly go back to minting and stepping a `DecodeStream`, and the suite would still pass. `to_scheduler_tests.rs` already matches `DetokMsg::Register { rid, .. }` in several places (e.g. L397); one of those could also assert `output_mode` for a `TokenIds` generate request.

A smaller gap of the same kind: the detokenizer test only covers a final chunk with a matched stop *token*. It doesn't exercise an intermediate (non-final) chunk or a `Matched::Str` stop in `TokenIds` mode.

                 rid: req.rid.clone(),
                 sink: req.sink.clone(),
                 decode_logprob_text,
+                output_mode: match &req.kind {
+                    RequestKind::Generate(g) => g.output_mode,
+                    _ => Default::default(),
+                },

nodes.body:
This comment was updated, but two others still describe `decoder == None` as meaning skip mode only:

- `DetokState.decoder` doc (L144): "`None` in `skip_tokenizer_init` mode"
- module doc (L16-18): only the `Skip` backend skips decoding

Both should be updated so nobody later treats `decoder.is_none()` as "no tokenizer available". For example, gating `decode_logprob_texts` on it would break token-only requests that still ask for logprob text.

Addressed in 05d2b763. The registration test now checks both output modes in `DetokMsg::Register`. The decoder test covers an intermediate chunk followed by terminal output for both token and string stops, and checks token IDs, counts, logprob text, empty token-only text, and request cleanup.

Addressed in 05d2b763. One exhaustive `RequestKind` match now sets all three registration flags. Generation keeps its requested mode; control and one-shot detokenization use `TokenIds`. One-shot decoding still uses the shared tokenizer. Tests check registration for both request types and retain response coverage.

nodes.body: Updated in 05d2b763. The module, backend, and decoder comments now explain that token-only requests skip the stream decoder. They also state that logprob-text decoding remains independent and uses the shared tokenizer.

Addressed in 05d2b763. `OutputMode` is imported directly, and the field documentation explains that `TokenIds` skips the stream decoder while stop-token trimming and logprob-text decoding remain independent.
